exposure: cervical length (CL) measured between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation
cohort: The cohort consisted of 874 pregnant women whose cervical length was measured between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation and who were followed until delivery.
finding: Measuring cervical length between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation can predict late and post-term pregnancy, with a CL above 35 mm significantly increasing the risk (5.8 times higher).
gest_age: Cervical length was measured between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation, with outcomes defined as late and post-term pregnancy (exceeding 38 weeks).
